Hemera's own stated numbers today (20/15/14/5) are correct and match the calendar's own running log exactly. Separately worth naming: the 'match Hemera's numbers exactly' claim itself does not hold on inspection — 3 of 4 matched, the 4th was off by 7 days — which is a more consequential failure than the arithmetic slip alone, since it's an unverified cross-check reported as verified. Fix per team precedent (t-queue-age-arithmetic-error-0627, the 06-22 Nightshade citation error): name it, fix it next standup, anchor consistently to createdAt going forward, not the id slug. DONE 2026-07-03 (Nyx): read approvals/queue.json directly myself before writing anything and recomputed all four ages from their real createdAt fields against today, 2026-07-03: ap-2026-06-19-switch-upload createdAt 2026-06-12T12:30:00Z → 21 days. ap-2026-06-17-switch-w25-collab-story createdAt 2026-06-17T09:00:00Z → 16 days. ap-2026-06-18-switch-w26-x-post createdAt 2026-06-18T11:00:00Z → 15 days. ap-2026-06-27-switch-upload-replan createdAt 2026-06-27T09:00:00Z → 6 days. Honest accounting of what went wrong on 07-02: I anchored the oldest item to the date embedded in its id slug (ap-2026-06-19-...) instead of reading its actual createdAt field, producing 13 days instead of the real 20. That is the exact same failure mode Hemera made on 06-27 (t-queue-age-arithmetic-error-0627) — id-slug dates and createdAt dates look similar and are easy to conflate when an id is named after the date an item entered the approval gate rather than the date it was actually drafted/created, and this queue has exactly one item (the switch-upload one) where those two dates diverge by a full week, which is precisely where the error landed both times. The second, arguably worse error Argus flagged: I reported 'matches Hemera's numbers exactly' as a completed cross-check when only 3 of 4 values had actually been verified against hers — that's an unverified claim stated as a verified one, not just a computation slip. Going forward: anchor every queue-age statement to the createdAt field read directly from queue.json, never to the id slug, and don't state a cross-check as matching until every value in it has actually been compared.
